summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Sharf earned his B.A. at the University of Toronto, studied at Kyoto University, and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez. His career includes posts at McMaster, Michigan, and UC Berkeley.
Hinde studied at St John's College (~1942–1948) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1950). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1950 to 1994.
Working in history and archaeology, Colebrooke was a member of The Asiatic Society (1785–1802) and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1794 to 1808.
Miller specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1955–1989) and at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kritzer completed his Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini by 1995. He was an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).
Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh and founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden in 1787.

Brown worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator in South and Southeast Asian art at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1980–2014) and as a professor at UCLA (~1986–2014).

Lenz, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Dorpat, Tartu, and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He taught at Tallinn Cathedral School, served in the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and was Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1836).

Gimello specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, earning his Ph.D. from Columbia University (~1969–1976). He was department head at the University of Arizona (~1981–2006) and a professor at Harvard University (~2001–2006).

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Maclagan studied at Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering. He served as Principal of IIT Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

A scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Magliola earned his Ph.D. at Princeton. He held professorships at Purdue, Assumption University, and National Taiwan University, along with positions at Tamkang University and Columbia University.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Mayer studied at the University of Bristol and Leiden University under Alexis Sanderson, Tilmann Vetter, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. In 2002, he joined the Oriental Studies faculty at the University of Oxford.

Cust was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Eton, Trinity College, Cambridge, East India Company College, and Fort William College. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.

Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, also training under traditional pandits. He became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley circa 1971.

Ellwood, a scholar of religious studies and Japanology, studied at Colorado, Yale, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He held a faculty position at the University of Southern California from circa 1967 to 1997.

A historian and archaeologist, Nelson studied at Rice University and New York University. He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) before taking a post at Yale University circa 2005.
Beekes, a linguist and Indologist, studied at Leiden University (~1955–1969) under F. B. J. Kuiper. He taught at Marnix Gymnasium (~1963–1968) and held posts at Leiden University in 1973 and 1979.
Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Sewell served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1868 to 1894 and as Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives from circa 1888 to 1894.
Conway was a linguist who studied at the City of London School. He held posts at Newnham College (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).
Clark works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao and doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang.
